# Colour {#sec-dd-colour}


::: {.cell}

:::


## Overview

Both the DVSA and DVLA sources record the vehicle's colour, but in different ways. The CARS pipeline keeps the values as
supplied and does not modify them.

- **`primaryColour_DVSA`** and **`secondaryColour_DVSA`** are the colours
  recorded in the MOT history.
- **`colour_DVLA`** is the colour on the DVLA register, as returned by the
  Vehicle Enquiry Service (VES).

Vehicles can change colour over time (although most don't). The DVSA do not provide a record of colour changes over time so the **`primaryColour_DVSA`** and **`secondaryColour_DVSA`** are likely to be the most recent values. The DVLA VES API also does not provide a record of colour changes over time, but repeated querying of the API may have found some vehicles that have changed colour. However in the main CARS outputs only the most recent colour is kept.

The DVSA and DVLA columns are described among the input data in the methodology,
[section 2](../../reports/methodology.md#input-data).

## Coverage

The DVSA primary colour is present for every vehicle and the secondary colour
for 91%. The secondary colour is less
often present for vehicles first used in 2023 and 2024
(41% for 2024) than for older or newer
ones (@fig-dd-colour). A value is not necessarily a colour, though: most
vehicles have the secondary colour `Not Stated` (@fig-dd-v-secondarycolour-dvsa),
so the column is not particularly useful.

The **`colour_DVLA`**, like every VES field, is present only where a VES record was
found: 77% of vehicles. When a vehicle does exist in the VES API it almost always has a colour value. The **`colour_DVLA`** is less present for those first used
before 2010, most of which have left the fleet and so are no longer included in the VES API (@sec-dd-dvla-status).
